source:
ParcelLink IE

ParcelLink: your parcel is held
at the depot. A EUR 3.49
redelivery fee is due today.
Pay to account PL-HOLD-8812
or the parcel is returned.
Do not reply to this number.

model_response.summary: A text message claims a parcel is held at a depot and demands an immediate EUR 3.49 redelivery fee to prevent return. It instructs payment to a specific account and explicitly tells the recipient not to reply to the number. These are classic tactics used in smishing (SMS phishing) campaigns targeting delivery customers.

red_flags.quote: your parcel is held at the depot. A EUR 3.49 redelivery fee is due today.
red_flags.why: The message creates artificial urgency by stating a fee is due today, pressuring the recipient to act quickly without verifying the claim.

red_flags.quote: Pay to account PL-HOLD-8812 or the parcel is returned.
red_flags.why: Demanding payment to a specific account to release a parcel is a common extortion tactic. Legitimate delivery services typically do not require immediate payment via unspecified accounts to release held items.

red_flags.quote: Do not reply to this number.
red_flags.why: Instructing the recipient not to reply is a red flag designed to prevent verification and limit the recipient's ability to confirm the message's legitimacy through direct contact.

safer_steps: Do not click any links or pay any fees mentioned in the message.

Contact the delivery company or retailer directly using independently verified contact details (e.g., from their official website or your order confirmation) to check if a redelivery fee is actually outstanding.
If you have recently ordered a parcel, check your order status and tracking information through the official retailer website or app.
Report the message as spam or phishing to your mobile provider if the option is available.
Delete the message and do not engage with the sender.

before_alignment_error: A quoted warning sign is not in the message.
